scientific_integrity: All global statements are analytic consequences of the published characteristic function, the ordinary central limit theorem, the inverse delta method, and explicit hyperbolic identities. The bundled numerical checks are regression tests rather than substitutes for the proof. Bibliographic noncoverage cannot exclude an equivalent calculation under unindexed residue-class or empirical-transform terminology.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns one single-frequency residue-class estimator for the one-parameter Cauchy–Cacoullos family. It proves uniform asymptotic-variance improvement only over the parity estimator analyzed in the motivating paper, not over maximum likelihood or optimally tuned multi-frequency empirical-characteristic-function procedures. The estimator requires an arbitrary finite-sample extension when its empirical transform is nonpositive; that event is eventually absent almost surely.
title: A modulo-three closed-form scale estimator for the Cauchy–Cacoullos family
